findings.note: The old quarter-coverage bug is fixed. Each logical fp32 element now has its own R32 texel write and read: four scalar float4(value) writes at (x+0..x+3, y) and four .x reads, with width 8 (small) / 512 (paper) and x+3 inside the row. The texture is a view of the same guarded scratch buffer, so the coverage read-back reads the actual scratch; the read-back covers all M*N scratch and output elements. The quarter negative is a real regression: the old single-coordinate float4 kernel leaves scratch holes and is detected at index 1, not via a self-reported flag.

The corrected probe and decision are sound. Texture arm: small 13.5858 us (+9.9708), paper 104.2154 us (+79.8258), 402.4648 GB/s; buffer arm: small 24.0550, paper 496.3208, 118.3111 GB/s with the timed fill. Decision: small hard 8.7713 us (4.806x) and probe 11.7960 (6.463x); paper hard 1211.4809 (1.0436x) and probe 1240.6939 (1.0688x); global_would_win=false. The corrected full-coverage texture arm did not accidentally make GLOBAL win; both small and paper remain far above REG and the REG route is unchanged.
